title: Mixed Conditionals / Mmusuo Adwumafo Mfiti
bridge: Wɔ Twi, mmusuo adwumafo mfiti nte sɛ wɔn ara nni: yɛnkyɛ yɛde mmusuo adwumafo a wɔbɔ ankasa a wɔde maa yɛbɔ mmusuo a ɛso wɔn ho asɛm no ho nhyehyɛe ne mmusuo a ɛso wɔn ho asɛm no ho nhyehyɛe. Wɔ Twiriso, mmusuo adwumafo a wɔbɔ ankasa no ho nhyehyɛe no, ɛsɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo kwan te sɛ: ɛsɛ ɛbɔ ɛpo mu kyerɛw (if-clause) ne ɛbɔ ɛpo mu kyerɛw (main clause) de mmusuo adwumafo a wɔbɔ ankasa no ho nhyehyɛe no, na ɛnyɛ sɛ nea obi a ɔde Twi kasa no bɔ. Mmusuo adwumafo a wɔbɔ ankasa no ho nhyehyɛe no, ɛsɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo kwan te sɛ: ɛsɛ wɔde mmusuo adwumafo a wɔbɔ ankasa no ho nhyehyɛe no de maa wo, na ɛnyɛ sɛ nea obi a ɔde Twi kasa no bɔ. Mmusuo adwumafo a wɔbɔ ankasa no ho nhyehyɛe no, ɛsɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo kwan te sɛ: ɛsɛ wɔde mmusuo adwumafo a wɔbɔ ankasa no ho nhyehyɛe no de maa wo, na ɛnyɛ sɛ nea obi a ɔde Twi kasa no bɔ.
rule: Mmusuo adwumafo mfiti no bɔ mmusuo a ɛwɔ awerɛho no ho nhyehyɛe ne mmusuo a ɛso wɔn ho asɛm no ho nhyehyɛe (type 3 + type 2) anaa mmusuo a ɛwɔ awerɛho no ho nhyehyɛe ne mmusuo a ɛso wɔn ho asɛm no ho nhyehyɛe (type 2 + type 3). Kyerɛw 1: If + past perfect, would + base verb (mmusuo a ɛwɔ awerɛho no ho nhyehyɛe, mmusuo a ɛso wɔn ho asɛm no ho nhyehyɛe). Kyerɛw: If I had studied harder, I would have a better job now. Kyerɛw 2: If + simple past, would have + past participle (mmusuo a ɛwɔ awerɛho no ho nhyehyɛe, mmusuo a ɛso wɔn ho asɛm no ho nhyehyɛe). Kyerɛw: If I were you, I would have told her the truth. Mmusuo: Wɔ mmusuo adwumafo mfiti no, ɛsɛ yɛde 'were' de εkyerɛ 'was' maa mmusuo a ɛwɔ awerɛho no ho nhyehyɛe no mu (If I were...). Na ɛpo mu kyerɛw no ho nhyehyɛe no, ɛbɔ ɛpo mu kyerɛw no ho nhyehyɛe no, na ɛnyɛ sɛ nea obi a ɔde Twi kasa no bɔ, nanso ɛsɛ wɔde koma de kyerɛw wo kwan te sɛ: ɛsɛ wɔde mmusuo a ɛwɔ awerɛho no ho nhyehyɛe no de maa wo. Mmusuo adwumafo mfiti no ho nhyehyɛe no, ɛsɛ yɛde kyerɛw wo kwan te sɛ: ɛsɛ wɔde mmusuo a ɛwɔ awerɛho no ho nhyehyɛe no de maa wo.

title: Advanced Passive Voice: Gerunds, Infinitives, and Modals / Nkyerɛasefoɔ a ɛyɛ den: Gerund, Infinitive ne Modals
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, nkyerɛasefoɔ a ɛyɛ den to to a wɔde 'be + past participle' ma no, na ɛnyɛ nea wɔde modal verbs anaa mmerɛa a ɛnyɛ nneɛma (gerund/infinitive) kyerɛw no. Wɔ English mu, nkyerɛasefoɔ a ɛyɛ den yɛ den sɛ: 'must be done', 'being done', 'to be done', etc. Mframa a ɛyɛ dɛn wɔ de Spanish kyerɛw no mu no, sɛdeɛ wɔbɛka 'debe ser hecho' nkyerɛkyerɛ 'has to be done'. Anaa, wɔ English mu, wɔtɔ agent no mfe (wɔnka 'by someone' sɛ ɛnyɛ paa), nanso wɔ Spanish mu, yɛde no dii.
rule: Wɔ English mu, nkyerɛasefoɔ a ɛyɛ den a ɛyɛ den no to to a wɔde 'to be' verb ma no wɔ mmerɛa kɛseɛ, modal anaa mmerɛa a ɛnyɛ nneɛma mu, na wɔde past participle kyerɛw no. Sɛ wɔde modal no ara na: modal + be + participle (sɛdeɛ 'must be done', 'can be seen'). Sɛ wɔde infinitive no ara na: to be + participle (sɛdeɛ 'to be considered'). Sɛ wɔde gerund no ara na: being + participle (sɛdeɛ 'being watched'). Sɛ wɔde perfect modal verbs no ara na: modal + have been + participle (sɛdeɛ 'should have been informed'). Na ɛsɛ wɔde preposition ma nkyerɛasefoɔ a ɛyɛ den no: 'This chair was sat on' (nanso ɛnyɛ nea wɔde dii). Fa akwantu sɛ wɔde intransitive verbs no kyerɛw anaa wɔtɔ agent no mfe: sɛ ɛnyɛ paa, tɔ no mfe. Wɔ Spanish mu, nkyerɛasefoɔ a ɛyɛ den no yɛ den pii, na wɔpɛ active voice anaa 'se' a ɛnyɛ nneɛma.

title: Advanced Reported Speech / Asɛm a ɛso ntɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka asɛm a ɛso ntɛm, yɛnkyɛ ahyɛdeɛ a ɛwɔ hɔ no sɛ yɛbɛka ɛno a ɛwɔ ɛkɛse no sɛ ɛyɛ ɛkɛse, nanso wɔ English, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɛka 'backshift' (siesie a ɛso ntɛm) sɛ ɛyɛ ɛkɛse sɛ ɛbɛka a ɛwɔ hɔ no ɛyɛ ɛkɛse: 'She says she is tired' vs. 'She said she was tired'. Anaa, wɔ English, nsiesie a ɛso ntɛm no yɛ ɛho nhia paa a wɔde bɛka asɛm a ɛso ntɛm no bi wɔ Twi: 'will' bɛyɛ 'would', 'can' bɛyɛ 'could', na mmienu a ɛwɔ ɛkɛse no nso bɛso (past simple → past perfect). Ntɛm baako a ɛyɛ den paa nso ɛne sɛ wɔ English, wɔmmusɛ subjunctive wɔ kyerɛw kronkron sɛm wɔ Twi ('Dijo que viniera' → 'He said to come' anaa 'He said that I should come'), na nsiesie a ɛso ntɛm no na sɛ wɔde bɛka adwene a ɛwɔ hɔ no yɛ ɛho nhia paa (today → that day, here → there).
rule:
Sɛ yɛbɛka asɛm a ɛso ntɛm wɔ English (B2 level):
1. **Backshift (siesie a ɛso ntɛm)**: Sɛ ɛbɛka a ɛwɔ hɔ no ɛyɛ ɛkɛse (said, told, asked), mmienu a ɛwɔ ɛbɛka a ɛso ntɛm no so ntɛm baako: present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; past simple → past perfect; present perfect → past perfect; will → would; can → could; may → might; must → had to (anaa must sɛ ɛyɛ ahyɛdeɛ a ɛho nhia).
2. **No backshift**: Nsiesie no nni sɛ asɛm no ka a ɛyɛ nokware anaa ɛho nhia wɔ ɛbɛka a ɛwɔ hɔ no (nanso ɛyɛ a wɔpɛ): 'He said he is ill' (sɛ ɔkyerɛ sɛ ɔwɔ hɔ) anaa 'He said he was ill' (sɛ ɛno a ɛnyɛ nokware).
3. **Nsiesie a ɛso aben a ɛwɔ hɔ na a wɔde bɛka**: Ntoa so sɛ ɛbɛyɛ: 'I' → 'he/she', 'my' → 'his/her', etc.
4. **Nsiesie a ɛso ntɛm na sɛ wɔde bɛka**: today → that day; yesterday → the day before / the previous day; tomorrow → the next day / the following day; here → there; now → then.
5. **Asɛm a ɛso ntɛm a ɛyɛ kyɛw**: Wɔtoa so sɛ ɛyɛ ɛkɛse na wɔde 'if/whether' bɛka a wɔde 'yes/no' na asɛm a ɛso ntɛm a ɛyɛ kyɛw no. Wɔmmusɛ auxiliary 'do/does/did': 'Where does he live?' → 'She asked where he lived.'
6. **Ahyɛdeɛ na kɔhwɛ**: Wɔde 'tell/ask + object + infinitive' bɛka: 'He told me to close the door.' Wɔmmusɛ 'that'.
7. **Mmienu a ɛho nhia**: 'would', 'could', 'might', 'should', 'ought to' no nsiesie. 'must' bɛka anaa bɛyɛ 'had to' so sɛ ɛbɛyɛ a ɛho nhia.

concept_examples.text: She said she had finished the report the day before.
concept_examples.translation: ɔkaa sɛ ɔde ɛto so no a ɛfiri ɛkɛse no ayɛɛ nhoma no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː sed ʃiː hæd ˈfɪnɪʃt ðə rɪˈpɔːrt ðə deɪ bɪˈfɔːr/

concept_examples.text: He asked if I could help him with the project.
concept_examples.translation: ɔbisaa sɛ ɔbɔɔ wɔ a wɔde bɛyɛ apam no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː æskt ɪf aɪ kʊd hɛlp hɪm wɪð ðə ˈprɒdʒɛkt/

concept_examples.text: They told us to wait outside.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔkaa yɛn sɛ yɛntena so.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ toʊld ʌs tə weɪt ˌaʊtˈsaɪd/

concept_examples.text: She warned that the meeting might be postponed.
concept_examples.translation: ɔkaa sɛ ɛbɛyɛ a wɔde bɛto so apam no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː wɔːrnd ðæt ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ maɪt biː poʊstˈpoʊnd/

common_error.wrong: She said me that she was tired.
common_error.correct: She told me that she was tired.
common_error.correct_alt: She said that she was tired.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, 'kaa' de ɛbɛka a wɔde bɛka a wɔde bɛka (me kaa), nanso wɔ English, 'say' no wɔhɔ a wɔde bɛka a wɔde bɛka; wɔde 'tell' bɛka sɛ wɔde bɛka a wɔde bɛka. Enti, 'said me' ɛnyɛ nokware; ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde 'told me' anaa 'said' bɛka a wɔmmusɛ a wɔde bɛka.

levels.label: Statements with Backshift
levels.translation: Asɛm a ɛyɛ nokware na ɛso ntɛm

examples.original: Paul said he was going to London the following day.
examples.phonetic: /pɔːl sɛd hiː wɒz ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ˈlʌndən ðə ˈfɒləʊɪŋ deɪ/
examples.translation: Paul kaa sɛ ɔbɛkɔ London ɛno a ɛbɛn.
examples.note: Hwɛ nsiesie no: 'is going' → 'was going' na 'tomorrow' → 'the following day'.

examples.original: She mentioned she had already seen that film.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˈmɛnʃənd ʃiː hæd ɔːlˈrɛdi siːn ðæt fɪlm/
examples.translation: ɔkaa sɛ ɔayɛɛ nhoma no.
examples.note: Present perfect 'have seen' so ntɛm baako a ɛyɛ ɛkɛse 'had seen'.

examples.original: They claimed they would finish the project by Friday.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ kleɪmd ðeɪ wʊd ˈfɪnɪʃ ðə ˈprɒdʒɛkt baɪ ˈfraɪdeɪ/
examples.translation: Wɔkaa sɛ wɔde bɛyɛ apam no a ɛbɛn.
examples.note: 'Will' bɛyɛ 'would' wɔ asɛm a ɛso ntɛm.

levels.label: Reported Questions
levels.translation: Asɛm a ɛso ntɛm a ɛyɛ kyɛw

examples.original: She asked where the nearest bank was.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː æskt wɛə ðə ˈnɪərɪst bæŋk wɒz/
examples.translation: ɔbisaa sɛ ɛhe na adwuma a ɛho nhia no wɔ.
examples.note: Wɔ asɛm a ɛso ntɛm a ɛyɛ kyɛw, ɛbɛyɛ ɛkɛse: 'was' wɔ ɛkɛse, ɛnyɛ 'was the bank'.

examples.original: He wondered if she had received his email.
examples.phonetic: /hiː ˈwʌndərd ɪf ʃiː hæd rɪˈsiːvd hɪz ˈiːmeɪl/
examples.translation: ɔbisaa sɛ ɔabaa ɛdɔm no.
examples.note: Sɛ ɛyɛ asɛm a ɛyɛ kyɛw a ɛyɛ 'yes/no', wɔde 'if' anaa 'whether' bɛka.

examples.original: They asked us why we hadn't called earlier.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ æskt ʌs waɪ wiː ˈhædnt kɔːld ˈɜːrliər/
examples.translation: Wɔbisaa yɛn sɛ yɛnntɔn aa yɛde bɛkɔ.
examples.note: Asɛm a ɛyɛ kyɛw no 'Why didn't you call?' bɛyɛ 'why we hadn't called'.

levels.label: Reported Commands, Requests and Suggestions
levels.translation: Ahyɛdeɛ, kɔhwɛ na asomdwoeɛ wɔ asɛm a ɛso ntɛm

examples.original: The teacher told us to stop talking.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈtiːtʃər toʊld ʌs tə stɒp ˈtɔːkɪŋ/
examples.translation: Kyerɛw no kaa yɛn sɛ yɛntena so.
examples.note: Wɔde 'tell + object + infinitive' bɛka ahyɛdeɛ.

examples.original: She asked me to open the window.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː æskt miː tə ˈəʊpən ðə ˈwɪndəʊ/
examples.translation: ɔkɔhwɛɛ me sɛ mɛbɔɔ ano no.
examples.note: Sɛ ɛyɛ kɔhwɛ, wɔde 'ask + object + infinitive' bɛka.

examples.original: He suggested going to the cinema.
examples.phonetic: /hiː səˈdʒɛstɪd ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə/
examples.translation: ɔsom aa wɔkɔ cinema.
examples.note: Sɛ ɛyɛ asomdwoeɛ, wɔde gerund (suggest + -ing) anaa 'that + should' bɛka.

examples.original: She recommended that we book early.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˌrɛkəˈmɛndɪd ðæt wiː bʊk ˈɜːrli/
examples.translation: ɔde ahyɛdeɛ maa yɛn sɛ yɛde yɛbɛtoa so.
examples.note: Sɛ ɛyɛ ahyɛdeɛ, wɔde 'that + clause' na ɛbɛyɛ ɛkɛse (subjunctive).

translations.tw: Asɛm a ɛso ntɛm a ɛho nhia

title: Inversion for Emphasis / Kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a, yɛnkyerɛ yɛmma abusuabɔ ne yɛde twi ne mmara pɛpɛɛpɛ a ɛyɛ kwan paa ("Nunca había visto algo así"). Nso wɔ English, sɛ wɔde mmerɛwo abo nea ɛyɛ den (rarely, not only, never, etc.) kɔso asɛm no, ɛsɛ wɔde ɔkɔmfo ne abofo no (anaa ɔkɔmfo 'to be') siesie wɔn nkuto wɔ asɛm no mu, sɛnea wɔde bɔ mmabɔ wɔ asɛm no mu hwehwɛ. Nhyehyɛe yi nni sɛ ɛyɛ adwuma: sɛ wode ayɛ no a, asɛm no te sɛ ɛyɛ nokware wɔ English kasa a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa. Mmara a ɔwɔ hɔ paa wɔ Hispanohablante no mu no, ɛne sɛ wɔde nhyehyɛe yi kɔ so, efisɛ wɔ Twi no mu no, nhyehyɛe sintaktiko yi nni hɔ.
rule: Kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho no ma wɔde abofo anaa kyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ asɛm no mu a ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ asɛm no mu. Nea ɛwɔ hɔ paa no, ɛne: never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever, not only, no sooner, little, under no circumstances, at no time, in no way. Nhyehyɛe no ne: [Kyerɛw a ɛyɛ den/kyerɛw a ɛyɛ den] + abofo (do/does/did, have/has, will, can, etc.) + ɔkɔmfo + ɔkɔmfo a ɔwɔ hɔ. Sɛ abofo no nni hɔ a, wɔde 'do' ma wɔn wɔ bere a ɛwɔ hɔ anaa 'did' wɔ bere a ɛda (gye 'to be', a wɔde no siesie wɔn nkuto wɔn ho). Wɔde 'not only' ma wɔn wɔ kyerɛw kwan so: "Not only did she sing, but she also danced". Wɔde 'no sooner' ma wɔn wɔ bere a ɛda a ɛwɔ hɔ so: "No sooner had we arrived than it started raining". Fenomeno yi yɛ nokware wɔ nhyehyɛe a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa anaa nhyehyɛe a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa, nso wɔde no wɔ kwan a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa ne kwan a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa.

concept_examples.text: Not only did she finish the project, but she also presented it brilliantly.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔno ara nni sɛ ɔde no ma no, nso ɔde no ma no pɛpɛɛpɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /nɒt ˈəʊnli dɪd ʃiː ˈfɪnɪʃ ðə ˈprɒdʒekt bʌt ʃiː ˈɔːlsəʊ prɪˈzentɪd ɪt ˈbrɪliəntli/

concept_examples.text: Rarely do we see such dedication in our team.
concept_examples.translation: Yɛnntɔn hɔ a yɛbɛka sɛ yɛbɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho wɔ yɛn akɔntɔfo mu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈreəli duː wiː siː sʌtʃ ˌdedɪˈkeɪʃn ɪn ˈaʊə tiːm/

concept_examples.text: Never have I encountered a more challenging problem.
concept_examples.translation: Mennto hɔ a mɛka sɛ mɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a ɛyɛ den paa.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈnevə hæv aɪ ɪnˈkaʊntəd ə mɔː ˈtʃælɪndʒɪŋ ˈprɒbləm/

concept_examples.text: Under no circumstances should you disclose this information.
concept_examples.translation: Wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no ma no, wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no ma no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈʌndə nəʊ ˈsɜːkəmstænsɪz ʃʊd juː dɪsˈkləʊz ðɪs ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃn/

common_error.wrong: Rarely we see such beautiful sunsets.
common_error.correct: Rarely do we see such beautiful sunsets.
common_error.correct_alt: We rarely see such beautiful sunsets.
common_error.explanation: Mmara no ma wɔde abofo a ɛyɛ den a ɛwɔ hɔ no kɔso asɛm no, ɛsɛ wɔde nhyehyɛe no ma wɔn wɔ abofo 'do' (wɔ bere a ɛwɔ hɔ) so. Kwan a ɛyɛ den paa a ɛwɔ hɔ no, ɛne sɛ wɔde abofo no ma wɔn wɔ ɔkɔmfo no ("We rarely see..."), a ɛne kwan a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa wɔ kasa a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa. Sɛ wubɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a, bu: sɛ abofo no wɔ kɔso a, ɛsɛ wode nhyehyɛe no ma no; sɛ wunnka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a, de abofo no ma no wɔ kwan biara so.

levels.label: Basic Inversion with Negative Adverbs
levels.translation: Kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a ɛyɛ den paa wɔ abofo a ɛyɛ den mu

examples.original: Never have I been so happy.
examples.phonetic: /ˈnevə hæv aɪ biːn səʊ ˈhæpi/
examples.translation: Mennto hɔ a mɛka sɛ mɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho.
examples.note: Wɔde 'have' ma wɔn wɔ abofo no so efisɛ bere a ɛwɔ hɔ no sɛ ɛyɛ paa a, ɛsɛ wɔde abofo no ma no. Wɔ Twi no mu no, 'nunca' te sɛ ɛwɔ hɔ wɔ ɔkɔmfo no mu a ɛnni nhyehyɛe biara.

examples.original: Hardly ever does he arrive on time.
examples.phonetic: /ˈhɑːdli ˈevə dʌz hiː əˈraɪv ɒn taɪm/
examples.translation: Ɔno ara nni hɔ a ɔbɛka sɛ ɔbɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho.
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛ wɔde 'he' (ɔkɔmfo a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa) ma no wɔ abofo 'does' so, ɛnnhyɛ 'do'.

examples.original: Little did we know about the plan.
examples.phonetic: /ˈlɪtəl dɪd wiː nəʊ əˈbaʊt ðə plæn/
examples.translation: Yɛnntɔn hɔ a yɛbɛka sɛ yɛbɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho.
examples.note: Abofo 'little' a ɛwɔ hɔ no a ɛyɛ den (poco) no ma nhyehyɛe no ma no. Wɔ Twi no mu no, wɔka 'poco sabíamos' a ɛnni nhyehyɛe biara.

levels.label: Inversion with 'Not Only' and 'No Sooner'
levels.translation: Kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho wɔ 'Not Only' ne 'No Sooner' mu

examples.original: Not only did they win the match, but they also broke the record.
examples.phonetic: /nɒt ˈəʊnli dɪd ðeɪ wɪn ðə mætʃ bʌt ðeɪ ˈɔːlsəʊ brəʊk ðə ˈrekɔːd/
examples.translation: Ɔno ara nni sɛ wɔde no ma no, nso wɔde no ma no pɛpɛɛpɛ.
examples.note: Nhyehyɛe no ma wɔn wɔ kyerɛw kwan so wɔ 'did' so. Kyerɛw a ɛwɔ hɔ no (but they also) nni nhyehyɛe.

examples.original: No sooner had the meeting started than the fire alarm went off.
examples.phonetic: /nəʊ ˈsuːnə hæd ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ ˈstɑːtɪd ðæn ðə ˈfaɪər əˈlɑːm went ɒf/
examples.translation: Ɔno ara nni hɔ a ɔbɛka sɛ ɔbɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a ɛyɛ den paa.
examples.note: Wɔde 'no sooner' ma wɔn wɔ bere a ɛda a ɛwɔ hɔ so (had + participio) ne nhyehyɛe no. Wɔ Twi no mu no, wɔde 'apenas' anaa 'no bien' a ɛnni nhyehyɛe biara.

examples.original: Not only is she intelligent, but she is also very creative.
examples.phonetic: /nɒt ˈəʊnli ɪz ʃiː ɪnˈtelɪdʒənt bʌt ʃiː ɪz ˈɔːlsəʊ ˈveri kriˈeɪtɪv/
examples.translation: Ɔno ara nni sɛ ɔyɛ den paa, nso ɔyɛ den paa pɛpɛɛpɛ.
examples.note: Wɔde 'to be' ma wɔn wɔ nhyehyɛe no so: wɔde ɔkɔmfo no ma no a ɛnni abofo 'do' biara.

levels.label: Advanced Inversion with Negative Prepositional Phrases
levels.translation: Kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa wɔ kyerɛw a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa mu

examples.original: Under no circumstances should you open that door.
examples.phonetic: /ˈʌndə nəʊ ˈsɜːkəmstænsɪz ʃʊd juː ˈəʊpən ðæt dɔː/
examples.translation: Wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no ma no, wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no ma no.
examples.note: Nhyehyɛe yi yɛ paa paa ne wɔde no wɔ nhyehyɛe, mmara anaa kyerɛw mu. Wɔ Twi no mu no, wɔka 'bajo ninguna circunstancia debes...' a ɛnni nhyehyɛe biara.

examples.original: At no time did the manager admit his mistake.
examples.phonetic: /æt nəʊ taɪm dɪd ðə ˈmænɪdʒər ədˈmɪt hɪz mɪˈsteɪk/
examples.translation: Wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no ma no, wɔn a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde no ma no.
examples.note: Kyerɛw 'at no time' no ma nhyehyɛe no ma no wɔ 'did' wɔ bere a ɛda so. Wɔ Twi no mu no, kwan a 'en ningún momento' wɔ no so yɛ den paa.

examples.original: In no way can we accept such a proposal.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn nəʊ weɪ kæn wiː əkˈsept sʌtʃ ə prəˈpəʊzl/
examples.translation: Yɛnntɔn hɔ a yɛbɛka sɛ yɛbɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho.
examples.note: Wɔde no ma wɔn wɔ abofo a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa, 'can', 'could', 'should'. Nhyehyɛe no ma wɔn wɔ abofo no so.

examples.original: Seldom have I seen such a magnificent performance.
examples.phonetic: /ˈseldəm hæv aɪ siːn sʌtʃ ə mæɡˈnɪfɪsənt pəˈfɔːməns/
examples.translation: Yɛnntɔn hɔ a yɛbɛka sɛ yɛbɛka ho kyerɛw ahwɛyɛho a ɛyɛ den paa.
examples.note: 'Seldom' yɛ ɔkɔmfo a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa a ɛte sɛ ɛyɛ paa. Wɔ Twi no mu no, wɔde 'rara vez' anaa 'raramente' a ɛnni nhyehyɛe biara.

title: Cleft sentences (It is/was... that) / Asɛm a ɛyɛ nea ɛte sɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛpɛ sɛ yɛfa akoma akyere kyɛ fa ko a, yɛnkyɛn yɛbɔ asɛm sɛ 'Na Juan a ɔyɛɛ no' anaa 'Na ɛyi a mete no'. Wɔ English, wɔbɔ no sɛ 'it' + 'to be' + nea wopɛ sɛ wofa akoma akyere no + 'that/who' + asɛm biara a ɛfiri so. Nnini a ɛte sɛ ne sɛ wɔ English no, ɛnsɛ sɛ woyɛ 'it' (ɛmpɛ sɛ wɔde no akɔ), na 'that' ne sɛ wɔde 'who' kaa akyire sɛ ɛyɛ mmofra, nanso ɛmpɛ sɛ wɔde 'which' kaa akyire wɔ nkyɛn yi. Enti, asɛm a wɔde bɔ no ho asɛm kom pɛn a wɔde bɔ no ho asɛm kom pɛn a wɔde bɔ no ho asɛm kom pɛn a wɔde bɔ no ho asɛm kom pɛn.
rule: Asɛm a ɛyɛ nea ɛte sɛ (cleft sentences) ne sɛ wɔde fa akoma akyere kyɛ fa ko a wɔ asɛm. Asɛm a ɛte sɛ ne sɛ: 'It' + 'to be' (wɔ berɛ a ɛte sɛ anaa a ɛnee) + nea wopɛ sɛ wofa akoma akyere no (sɛnea ɛte sɛ, sɛnea ɛyɛ, sɛnea ɛte sɛ, sɛnea ɛte sɛ, etc.) + pronombre relativo ('that', 'who', 'whom', 'whose') + asɛm biara a ɛfiri so. Sɛ ɛyɛ mmofra a, ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔde 'who' (sɛnea ɛte sɛ) anaa 'whom' (sɛnea ɛyɛ, nanso ɛyɛ formal). Sɛ ɛyɛ nnuan nea ɛfiri so a, ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔde 'that' (anaa 'which' wɔ formal). Wɔ berɛ a ɛte sɛ, wɔde 'is', wɔ berɛ a ɛnee, wɔde 'was'. Wɔmmusɛ 'it's' wɔ berɛ a ɛnee (ɛyɛ ɛha), wɔde 'it was'. Nea wopɛ sɛ wofa akoma akyere no ne sɛ ɛyɛ noun, pronombre, frase preposicional anaa sɛ ɛyɛ cláusula. Sɛnea ɛte sɛ: 'It was Maria who called me.' / 'It is the weekend that I enjoy the most.' / 'It was in Paris that we met.' / 'It is because of you that I came.' Wɔ nea ɛfiri so, wɔwɔ hɔ 'what' (what-clauses): 'What I need is a coffee.' Wɔ nkyɛn yi, wɔmmusɛ 'it' sɛ ɛyɛ subject, nanso wɔde 'what' kaa akyire. Nea ɛfiri so: 'The reason why...', 'The thing that...', 'The person who...', nanso nea ɛte sɛ ne 'it' ne 'what'. Nnini: wɔmmusɛ 'it' sɛ ɛyɛ nea ɛte sɛ (wɔde nea ɛfiri so kaa akyire sɛ 'what...do'). Wɔ negations, wɔde 'It wasn't...' anaa 'It isn't...'.

title: Nominalisation: Turning Verbs and Adjectives into Nouns / Nominalización: Kyerɛw Kronkron ne Nnɔmba mu Nnɔnhweɛfoɔ
bridge: Wɔ Wiase nyimpa twitwa mu, nominalization yɛ nkwa pɛ wɔ nwoma kwan so ne akwan akɔntɔ a ɛtɔ da biara: 'the discovery of' yɛ deɛ wɔpɛ sen 'they discovered'. Ɛfiri dwuma a ɛyɛ wɔ Espane, wɔnom nnɔnhweɛfoɔ wɔ mmerɛ a ɛwɔ hɔ bio (el descubrir), Wiase nyimpa twitwa de mmara -tion, -ment, -ness. Hwɛ da: mmara wɔn nyinaa nni nnɔnhweɛfoɔ a ɛfiri asɛm a ɛyɛ nea ɛde kyerɛw kronkron, na nsɛm a ɛde kyerɛw kronkron so rekɔ: wɔ Wiase nyimpa twitwa mu, ɛsɛe a wɔde kyerɛw kronkron (an aa ɛyɛ 'of') rekɔ nnɔnhweɛfoɔ, na wɔ Espane mu, wɔde 'de' maa ɛkɔ so.
rule:
Ma B2, hwɛ mmara yi:
1. Mmara kyerɛw kronkron → nnɔnhweɛfoɔ: -tion (inform → information), -ment (develop → development), -ance/-ence (perform → performance), -al (approve → approval), -ure (fail → failure).
2. Mmara nnɔmba → nnɔnhweɛfoɔ: -ness (happy → happiness), -ity (active → activity), -th (strong → strength), -ce (important → importance).
3. Mmara a wɔn ho ntumi nhwɛ: choose → choice, believe → belief, prove → proof, lose → loss.
4. Deɛ ɛsɛ: wɔ Wiase nyimpa twitwa a ɛtɔ da biara mu, wɔpɛ 'the implementation of the plan' sen 'they implemented the plan'. Kɔ so mmara 'make' + nnɔnhweɛfoɔ: 'make a decision' na ɛnni 'decide'.
5. Mmara a wɔn ho nhwɛ: mmara kyerɛw kronkron koma wɔn mu biara nni nnɔnhweɛfoɔ (change → change), na nnɔnhweɛfoɔ koma wɔn mu biara wɔ kyerɛw a ɛfiri asɛm a ɛyɛ (relation vs. relationship).

title: Advanced Modal Verbs: Would Have, Should Have, etc. / Modales tɔso: would have, should have, etc.
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛbɛka nhyehyɛe nnɛm-nnɛm yi ne kondisional kɔmposo (sɛ ɛbɛyɛ, sɛ ɛbɛhyɛ) anaa ne subjuntivo ɛtɔ. Nanso, wɔ Gyeman mu, wɔde modals (would, should, could, might) ne 'have' ne past participle kɔm. Nnipa no ara ne sɛ, wɔ Twi mu yɛde 'haber' + participle, nanso wɔ Gyeman mu, nnipa no ne modal + 'have' + participle. Faako: 'would have' nteaseɛ, ɛnte sɛ 'ɛbɛyɛ' ɛho nhia, nanso ɛka kondisional ɛkɔ wɔ awa mu.
rule: Wɔde modal (would, should, could, might, must) + 'have' + past participle. Wɔde yi ka nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ awa mu (would have), anaa nhwɛso a wɔannyɛ (should have), anaa nnwuma a ɛnyɛ (could have, might have), anaa nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ awa mu (must have). Wɔ ne-gyinae mu, de 'not' kɔ modal hɔ (should not have / shouldn't have). Wɔ hwɛso mu, fa sofo no kyerɛw (Would you have...?). Kyerɛw nnipa: would've, should've, could've. Nnkyerɛaseɛ: 'must have' nni hɔ ma wɔde ka nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ awa mu (de 'couldn't have' anaa 'was not allowed to').

examples.note: 'Might have' ka nnwuma a ɛwɔ awa mu, na ɛnyɛ ɛho nhyehyɛe.

examples.original: She must have been very tired after the trip.

examples.note: 'Must have' ka nhyehyɛe a ɛwɔ awa mu.

examples.note: Ma wɔde 'couldn't have' nea ɛho nhyehyɛe no, wɔde 'mustn't have'.

title: Participle Clauses / Nsɛmfa a wɔde participle bɔɔ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyɛ yɛbɔ nsɛmfa a wɔde 'mientras', 'como', 'ya que' anaa 'después de que' kyerɛw wɔ kyerɛw wɔde verb biara. Wɔ English, sɛ wopɛ sɛ nsɛm no bɛyɛ formal paa na yɛn ntɛm, wɔde participle clause (present anaa past) kaa nsɛmfa no ho. Nkɔso biara a ɛwɔ hɔ no, wɔ English no, nsɛmfa no ne participle clause no sujet bi ara na ɛsɛ; sɛ ɛnyɛ nkonim, ɛbɛma yɛfa 'dangling participle' (participle a ɛte) a ɛte paa. Afei, Twi mmom a ɛma yɛn pɛ sɛ yɛbɔ gerund ('caminando por la calle, vi...'), nanso wɔ English no, participle present ('walking down the street, I saw...') no wɔ hɔ a wɔde bɔɔ no wɔ kyerɛw a wɔde 'having' bɔɔ no.
rule: Participle clauses no wɔ hɔ a wɔde participle present (-ing) anaa participle past (-ed anaa irregular form) bɔɔ no. Wɔde wɔ kyerɛw time (mientras, después de), cause (porque, ya que), condition (si), anaa concession (aunque). Participle clause no yɛ den a ɛwɔ nsɛm no anim anaa sujet no nkyɛn, na nsɛmfa no sujet ne participle no sujet bi ara. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wode kyerɛw action a ɛda no ho a, wɔde 'having + participio pasado' (e.g., 'Having finished my homework, I went out'). Wɔ passive voice no, wɔde 'being + participio pasado' (e.g., 'Being late, I missed the bus'). Afei, wɔde wɔ nouns nkyɛn a wɔde kaa relative clauses (e.g., 'the man sitting there' = 'the man who is sitting there'). Wɔmmusɛ wɔ sujets a wɔnyɛ biara; wɔ nhwɛso no, sɛ wo ne nsɛm bi a ɛne participle clause no sujet bi, εna εyɛ sɛ wode conjunction (while, because, etc.) ne sujet a ɛte.

concept_examples.text: Walking down the street, I saw an old friend.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛberɛ a mewuo mu, memfa nyansa biara.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈwɔːkɪŋ daʊn ðə striːt, aɪ sɔː ən əʊld frend/

concept_examples.text: Having finished her work, she went home.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛberɛ a ɔdaadaa no ayɛ, ɔdaa no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈhævɪŋ ˈfɪnɪʃt hɜː wɜːk, ʃiː went həʊm/

concept_examples.text: The man sitting over there is my boss.
concept_examples.translation: Ono a ɔte wɔ hɔ no ne me boss.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə mæn ˈsɪtɪŋ ˈəʊvə ðeə ɪz maɪ bɒs/

concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈbiːɪŋ ˈtaɪəd, aɪ dɪˈsaɪdɪd tə ɡəʊ tə bed ˈɜːli/

common_error.wrong: Walking down the street, the church was seen.
common_error.correct: Walking down the street, I saw the church.
common_error.correct_alt: While I was walking down the street, I saw the church.
common_error.explanation: Nkɔso no ne 'dangling participle' (participle a ɛte): clause no 'walking down the street' no sujet mmom mmom nsɛmfa no sujet ('the church'). Wɔ Twi no, yɛnkyɛ yɛbɔ passive, nanso wɔ English no ɛyɛ nkɔso. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woafo no, ma nsɛmfa no sujet ne participle clause no sujet bi ara. Sɛ ɛnyɛ nkonim, sɛ wo ne nsɛm bi a ɛne 'while', 'because', etc.

levels.label: Present Participle Clauses
levels.translation: Participle present clauses

examples.original: Feeling hungry, I made a sandwich.
examples.phonetic: /ˈfiːlɪŋ ˈhʌŋɡri, aɪ meɪd ə ˈsænwɪdʒ/
examples.translation: Ɛberɛ a me te ahwɛ, mede me ho adwene.
examples.note: Participle present (-ing) no kyerɛw cause anaa time a ɛte saa. Wɔ Twi no, yɛnkyɛ yɛde gerund anaa 'como' + verb bɔɔ.

examples.original: She left the room crying.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː left ðə ruːm ˈkraɪɪŋ/
examples.translation: Ɔfaa baabi no anim a ɔte ahwɛ.
examples.note: Sɛ participle no wɔ verb no nkyɛn a, ɛkyerɛw mode anaa accompaniment. Nhwɛso: wɔ English no, wɔmmusɛ 'she left crying' sɛ ɛte sɛ ɔte ahwɛ a ɔte baa no; ɛte saa.

examples.original: While waiting for the bus, I read a book.
examples.phonetic: /waɪl ˈweɪtɪŋ fə ðə bʌs, aɪ red ə bʊk/
examples.translation: Ɛberɛ a mɛfaa trotro no, mɛkenkan.
examples.note: Yɛnkyɛ yɛde 'while' + participle a yɛbɔɔ no a yɛkyerɛkyerɛ simultaneity. Sɛ 'while' nni hɔ a, ɛyɛ nkɔso, nanso 'while' no ma time relation no te.

levels.label: Past Participle Clauses
levels.translation: Participle past clauses

examples.original: Frightened by the noise, the cat hid under the bed.
examples.phonetic: /ˈfraɪtnd baɪ ðə nɔɪz, ðə kæt hɪd ˈʌndə ðə bed/
examples.translation: Ɛberɛ a ɔte ahwɛ a, ɔmaa no ani.
examples.note: Participle past no wɔ hɔ a wɔde kyerɛw passive anaa state. Wɔ hɔ no 'frightened' no ne adjective a ɛde sujet no state kyerɛw.

examples.original: Given more time, I could finish the project.
examples.phonetic: /ˈɡɪvn mɔː taɪm, aɪ kʊd ˈfɪnɪʃ ðə ˈprɒdʒekt/
examples.translation: Sɛ woma me more time a, mɛbɔ project no.
examples.note: ɛkyerɛw condition (si + passive). Wɔ Twi no, yɛde 'si' + subjunctive anaa 'dado más tiempo' bɔɔ.

examples.original: The window broken in the storm has been repaired.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈwɪndəʊ ˈbrəʊkən ɪn ðə stɔːm hæz biːn rɪˈpeəd/
examples.translation: Window a ɛbrɛɛ wɔ anantɛm no ho no asɛm no ayɛ.
examples.note: Sɛ ɛyɛ noun modifier a, participle past no de kaa relative clause a ɛyɛ passive.

levels.label: Perfect Participle Clauses
levels.translation: Participle perfect clauses

examples.original: Having missed the train, we had to take a taxi.
examples.phonetic: /ˈhævɪŋ mɪst ðə treɪn, wiː hæd tə teɪk ə ˈtæksi/
examples.translation: Ɛberɛ a yɛbrɛɛ train no a, yɛmaa taxi bi.
examples.note: Wɔde 'having + participio pasado' a wɔkyerɛw action a ɛda no ho. Wɔ Twi no, yɛde 'habiendo perdido' anaa 'como perdimos' bɔɔ.

examples.original: Not having studied enough, she failed the exam.
examples.phonetic: /nɒt ˈhævɪŋ ˈstʌdɪd ɪˈnʌf, ʃiː feɪld ði ɪɡˈzæm/

examples.note: Negative form no wɔ hɔ a wɔde 'not' bɔɔ 'having' anim. Wɔ Twi no, yɛde 'no habiendo' anaa 'como no estudió' bɔɔ.

examples.original: Having been warned about the storm, they stayed home.
examples.phonetic: /ˈhævɪŋ biːn wɔːnd əˈbaʊt ðə stɔːm, ðeɪ steɪd həʊm/
examples.translation: Ɛberɛ a wɔkyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ anantɛm bɛba a, wɔdaa wɔn fi mu.
examples.note: Passive perfect form no ne 'having been + participio pasado'. Ɛyɛ formal na wɔde wɔ writing anaa speeches.

title: Formal Subjunctive / Subjuntivo formal (wɔ ne sɛ ɔyɛ...)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, subjuntivo wɔ adwuma a ɔwɔ kwan so na ɛwɔ mmerɛwa a wɔhyɛ da biara. Wɔ English, formal subjuntivo (anaa mandative subjunctive) amfa nnie kan a wɔbɛka ho asɛm wɔ nnipa a wɔkasa ne wɔn a wɔyɛ akwantufoɔ mpo mu, ɛno a ɛwɔ akyi a wɔbɛka 'it is essential that...', 'I demand that...' anaa 'the doctor recommended that...'. Sɛnea ɛte Twi, English subjuntivo nko ara na wɔhu ɛwɔ ɛho a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ akyi (be na ɛnnye is) ne wɔ be kyerɛw (I be, you be, he be). Hispanohablantes pii wɔ a wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka indicative ('he is') efisɛ ɛne English a wɔkasa no ho asɛm da, nanso wɔ akwan a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm no, wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka subjuntivo.
rule: English formal subjuntivo de wɔ akyi a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ akyi a wɔbɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm, a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm, anaa a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm. Sɛnea ɛte: 'that + ɔkyerɛw + kyerɛw wɔ ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so' (infinitive without 'to'). Wɔnnhyɛ -s wɔ ɛho a ɔwɔ akyi a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ akyi. 'Be' kyerɛw de wɔ ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so 'be' maa wɔn nyinaa. Wɔde ɛno maa wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm, 'demand', 'insist', 'recommend', 'suggest', 'ask', 'require', na wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm, 'essential', 'important', 'necessary', 'vital', 'crucial', anaa ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so, 'requirement', 'suggestion'. Sɛnea ɛte Twi, ɛwɔ akyi a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm (hable, hables, hable...), English nko ara na ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so. Wɔ mmerɛwa a wɔnnyɛ akwan, nnipa a wɔkasa no wɔ akyi a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm (he goes, it is), nanso wɔ akwan a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm no, wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka subjuntivo. Wɔde 'should' maa ɛno (It is essential that he should be), nanso ɛne British na ɛwɔ akwan. English subjuntivo de wɔ akyi a wɔde bɛka 'lest' (raro) na wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm 'God save the Queen'.

concept_examples.text: It is essential that he be present at the meeting.

concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ɪˈsɛnʃəl ðæt hi bi ˈprɛzənt æt ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: I demand that you be honest with me.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛbɔ ɔhaw mu sɛ woyɛ honesto ma me.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ dɪˈmɑːnd ðæt juː bi ˈɒnɪst wɪð miː/

concept_examples.text: It is crucial that the data be verified before publication.
concept_examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɛyɛ data no a wɔde bɛto so no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈkruːʃəl ðæt ðə ˈdeɪtə bi ˈvɛrɪfaɪd bɪˈfɔː ˌpʌblɪˈkeɪʃən/

common_error.wrong: It is essential that he is present at the meeting.
common_error.correct: It is essential that he be present at the meeting.
common_error.explanation: Ɛbɔ a ɛbɔ efisɛ Twi subjuntivo wɔ ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so (esté), na students no pɛ sɛ wɔbɛka English indicative 'is' a ɛte sɛ ɛne wɔn a wɔkasa no. Nanso, wɔ English formal subjuntivo no, kyerɛw no sɛ ɛwɔ ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so (be) na ɛnnye person flexion. Ma wɔawo no, yɛbɛka sɛ akyi a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm anaa a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm, kyerɛw no wɔ 'that' clause no mu daa wɔ ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so, na ɛnnye -s, ɛne he/she/it. Yɛbɛyɛ adwuma a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm maa indicative maa subjuntivo.

levels.label: After adjectives of necessity
levels.translation: Akyi a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm

examples.original: It is important that she attend the conference.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ɪmˈpɔːtənt ðæt ʃi əˈtɛnd ðə ˈkɒnfərəns/
examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ ɔbɛwɔ conference no mu.
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛ 'attend' nnye -s ɛne sɛ ɔkyerɛw no ne 'she'. Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka 'asista', entɛ sɛ ɛne ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so.

examples.original: It is necessary that every student bring their own laptop.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈnɛsəsəri ðæt ˈɛvri ˈstjuːdənt brɪŋ ðeər oʊn ˈlæptɒp/
examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ student no bɛfa laptop no.
examples.note: Wɔ hɛn, 'student' ne singular, nanso 'bring' nnye -s efisɛ ɛne subjuntivo. Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka 'traiga'.

examples.original: It is vital that the team communicate clearly.

examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ team no bɛka ho asɛm.

levels.label: After verbs of recommendation or demand
levels.translation: Akyi a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm anaa a wɔde bɛka a wɔwɔ ho asɛm

examples.original: The manager insists that employees use the new software.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈmænɪdʒər ɪnˈsɪsts ðæt ˌɛmplɔɪˈiːz juːz ðə njuː ˈsɒftweər/
examples.translation: Manager no kaa sɛ employees no bɛfa software no.
examples.note: Wɔ hɛn, 'insists' ne kyerɛw a ɛwɔ kwan so, nanso wɔ subordinate clause no mu, yɛbɛka 'use' wɔ ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so.

examples.original: They demanded that she apologize immediately.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ dɪˈmɑːnd ðæt ʃi əˈpɒlədʒaɪz ɪˈmiːdiətli/
examples.translation: Wɔkaa sɛ ɔmfa adanse daa.
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛ main time no ne past ('demanded'), nanso subjuntivo no daa wɔ kyerɛw a ɛwɔ kwan so 'apologize'. Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka 'se disculpara' (imperfect subjuntivo).

examples.original: I suggest that he take a break.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ səˈdʒɛst ðæt hi teɪk ə breɪk/
examples.translation: Meka sɛ ɔbɛfa break.
examples.note: Wɔ Twi, 'tome' ne present subjuntivo; wɔ English, 'take' ne ɛho a ɛwɔ kwan so.

levels.label: Formal and academic contexts
levels.translation: Mmerɛwa a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm na akwantufoɔ

examples.original: The committee recommended that the proposal be rejected.
examples.phonetic: /ðə kəˈmɪti ˌrɛkəˈmɛndɪd ðæt ðə prəˈpoʊzəl bi rɪˈdʒɛktɪd/

examples.note: Wɔ hɛn, 'be' ne subjuntivo a wɔde bɛka 'to be'. Passive voice 'be rejected' daa wɔ subjuntivo.

examples.original: It is essential that the contract be signed by Friday.

examples.translation: Ɛsɛ sɛ contract no bɛto so.
examples.note: Subjuntivo 'be' de wɔn a wɔkasa no ho asɛm 'is'. Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka 'sea' (present subjuntivo).

examples.original: The regulations require that each member be notified in writing.

examples.translation: Regulations no ka sɛ member no bɛto so.
examples.note: Wɔ Twi, 'sea notificado' ne subjuntivo. Wɔ English, 'be' de ɛno.

title: Future Perfect and Continuous / Anigye Pefee ne Anigye Nkyerε
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka anigye kyerεw kronkron ma adwuma a ɛbɛyɛ anansesεm wɔ anigye mu, nanso ɛha English no yɛ nkyerεmmarima a wɔwɔ hɔ a wɔde kyerε adwuma a ɛbɛyɛ pefee anaa ɛrekɔ so wɔ anigye kyerεw mu. Anigye pefee (will have + past participle) te sε 'habré + participio' wɔ Twi, nanso hwε: wɔ Twi, yɛnka anigye kyerεw kronkron ma mmom wɔ nnipa mmienu, na wɔ English no, ɛyɛ nokware a ɛsɛ sε yɛbɛyɛ ɛha. Nokware foforo nso ɛha sε anigye nkyerε (will be + -ing) nni ɛha wɔ Twi; yɛnka mmara sε 'estaré haciendo' anaa yɛnka anigye kyerεw kronkron, na yɛde ɛha a ɛrekɔ so.
rule: Wɔ English no, anigye pefee yɛ 'will have' + past participle na yɛde ma adwuma a ɛbɛyɛ pefee ansa na anigye kyerεw mu. Kyekye: 'By 2025, I will have finished my degree.' Anigye nkyerε yɛ 'will be' + verb in -ing na yɛde ma adwuma a ɛrekɔ so wɔ anigye kyerεw mu. Kyekye: 'At 8 p.m., I will be having dinner.' Yɛde ma adwuma a ɛbɛyɛ anansesεm anaa a yɛbɛyɛ wɔ anigye, na sε yɛbɛbua dwuma wɔ anigye mu. Wɔ asεm a ɛwɔ hɔ a ɛte 'when', 'as soon as', 'until', yɛnka present tense na ɛnni anigye pefee anaa anigye nkyerε: 'When you arrive, I will have cooked dinner.' Anigye pefee nkyerε (will have been + -ing) yɛ ɛha a ɛso awaree na yɛde ma adwuma a ɛrekɔ so wɔ anigye kyerεw mu: 'By June, I will have been living here for six months.' Nnipa a wɔyɛ nnɔɔso: mmom 'will' wɔ asεm a ɛwɔ hɔ a ɛte; mmom anigye pefee ma adwuma a ɛrekɔ so; na mmom past participle ne past tense.

concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi wɪl hæv bɪn ˈwɜːrkɪŋ hɪr fɔːr faɪv jɪrz baɪ tuː ˈθaʊzənd ənd ˈtwɛnti sɪks/

title: Discourse Markers for Cohesion / Nkyerɛntoro asɛm a wɔde ma asɛm ka ho ntɔ so
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nkyerɛntoro asɛm (sɛ 'nanso', 'na', 'nkyɛn') mpo a, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw wo asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te. Wɔ English, nkyerɛntoro asɛm pii a wɔde ma asɛm ka ho ntɔ so wɔ hɔ a wɔn ho nhia so ara na wɔwɔ hɔ a, wɔn kyerɛw no ne nnipa a wɔde kasa no so ntɛm. Sɛ 'however' (nanso) ne 'although' (nkyɛn) a, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te. 'However' (nanso) ne 'so' (na) a, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te: 'so' yɛ akwan akɔsoɔ na wɔde kasa, 'therefore' (na) yɛ akwan akɔsoɔ na wɔde kyerɛw.
rule: Nkyerɛntoro asɛm wɔ English (B2) wɔ hɔ a wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ: aditivos (furthermore, moreover, in addition), de contraste (however, nevertheless, on the other hand, whereas), de causa/efecto (therefore, consequently, as a result, thus), de secuencia (firstly, secondly, finally, meanwhile), na de reformulación (in other words, that is to say). Nnipa a wɔde kasa no: 1) 'However' yɛ kyerɛw na wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ; wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te. Sɛ: 'The weather was bad. However, we went out.' / 'The weather was bad. We went out, however.' 2) 'Although' yɛ kyerɛw a wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ; wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te: 'Although it was raining, we went out' (wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ). 3) 'Therefore' na 'consequently' yɛ akwan akɔsoɔ, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te; 'so' yɛ akwan akɔsoɔ na wɔde kasa. 4) 'On the other hand' wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te, nanso wɔnni 'however' (a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te). 5) Wɔ English, kyerɛw yɛ den: sɛ wɔde 'however' kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te a, wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ. 6) Nkyerɛntoro asɛm a wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ ('firstly', 'secondly', 'finally') wɔ hɔ a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te. Sɛ wɔ Twi a, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te.

concept_examples.text: The company expanded rapidly; however, it failed to maintain quality.
concept_examples.translation: Kumpani no ahyɛde ahyɛ a, nanso wɔnni akwan a wɔde ma wɔn ho ntɔ so.

common_error.wrong: It was raining, however, we went to the beach.
common_error.correct: It was raining; however, we went to the beach.
common_error.correct_alt: It was raining. However, we went to the beach.
common_error.explanation: Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔ Twi a, wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te, sɛ 'Ɔyɛɛ no, nanso, yɛde no ma yɛn ho ntɔ so'. Nanso wɔ English a, 'however' nni kyerɛw a wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ, na wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te. Wɔde wɔn akɔsoɔ (;) anaa ɔkɔm (.) a wɔde 'however' kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te. Suhyɛ 'however' (a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te) ne 'although' (a wɔde wɔn kyerɛw asɛm no mu ansa na wɔde wɔn hwɛ kwan te): 'Although it was raining, we went' yɛ den, nanso 'Although it was raining, however, we went' nni den (redundante).

translations.tw: Nkyerɛntoro asɛm a wɔde ma asɛm ka ho ntɔ so

title: Hedging Language / Asɛm a ɛsɔ hwɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyɛ yɛnka subjunctive anaa asɛm bɛka 'parece que' maa yɛbɛka yɛn ani a yɛnnyɛ sure. Wɔ English, hedging yɛ ma wɔka modal verbs, adverbs na expressions a wɔde maa asɛm a wɔrekɛ bɛka no mmɔ. Sɛe wɔde 'tiendo a' ka 'tend to' ho nhia nkyerɛaseɛ biara, anaa wɔde 'apparently' ka 'seemingly' a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔka no. Wɔn a wɔbɛka English no bɛtumi tu asɛm a wɔbɛka no sɛnea wɔn a wɔde no ase bɛka no ka, na wɔmmusua asɛm a ɛto so anaa a wɔrekɛ sure.
rule: Wɔ English, hedging yɛ ma wɔde maa wɔbɛka wɔn ani a wɔnnyɛ sure, anaa wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛyɛ general. Wɔde nnɛm: 1) Modal verbs: may, might, could, can. Kyekye: 'It might rain' (Ebia ɛbɔ). 2) Adverbs a wɔde maa wɔbɛka wɔn ani a wɔnnyɛ sure: usually, generally, apparently, presumably. Kyekye: 'Apparently, he left early' (Sɛnea yɛte nteaseɛ no, ɔfɔɔ). 3) Verbs a wɔde maa wɔbɛka wɔn ani a wɔnnyɛ sure: I think, I believe, I suppose, I tend to think. Kyekye: 'I tend to agree with you' (Mɛtumi aba a mɛkɔ so). 4) Impersonal expressions: It seems that, It appears that, It is said that. Kyekye: 'It seems that she is tired' (Sɛnea yɛte nteaseɛ no, ɔyɛ adwuma). 5) Structures a wɔde 'tend to' + infinitive maa wɔbɛka habits anaa tendencies. Kyekye: 'He tends to arrive late' (Ɔsɔ hwɛ a ɔbɛba paa). 6) 'Apparently' yɛ ma wɔde maa wɔbɛka asɛm a wɔte nteaseɛ no, na 'seemingly' yɛ ma wɔde maa wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛyɛ sɛnea ɛte nteaseɛ no. 7) 'Rather' na 'quite' tumi maa adjectives mmɔ. Kyekye: 'It's rather expensive' (ɛyɛ paa). 8) Wɔ academic contexts, wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka 'would seem' anaa 'could be argued' maa wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛyɛ formal. Faako a, wɔ Twi, yɛde subjunctive akyerɛ 'parece que', nanso wɔ English, wɔde indicative: 'It seems that he is sick' (Sɛnea yɛte nteaseɛ no, ɔyɛ adwuma).

common_error.wrong: I think that the project is feasible.
common_error.correct: I tend to think that the project is feasible.
common_error.correct_alt: It seems to me that the project is feasible.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, 'pienso que' yɛ asɛm a wɔde maa wɔbɛka wɔn ani a wɔnnyɛ sure, nanso wɔ English, 'I think' tumi aba a ɛyɛ too strong wɔ formal contexts anaa sɛ wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛsɔ hwɛ. Ɛyɛ sɛe sɛ wɔde Twi ka English. Sɛ wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka hedging, wɔtumi de 'I tend to think', 'I would say', anaa 'I suppose' maa wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛsɔ hwɛ. Mmom sɛ wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛyɛ cautious anaa academic, wɔmmusua 'I think'.

levels.label: Adverbs of Uncertainty
levels.translation: Adverbs a wɔde maa wɔbɛka wɔn ani a wɔnnyɛ sure

examples.original: Apparently, the flight has been delayed.
examples.phonetic: /əˈpærəntli ðə flaɪt hæz biːn dɪˈleɪd/
examples.translation: Sɛnea yɛte nteaseɛ no, ɛflight no a wɔdelay no.
examples.note: Wɔde 'apparently' sɛ asɛm no fi baabi a ɛnni wɔn ho.

examples.original: Presumably, he has already finished the report.
examples.phonetic: /prɪˈzjuːməbli hiː hæz ɔːlˈrɛdi ˈfɪnɪʃt ðə rɪˈpɔːt/
examples.translation: Sɛnea yɛte nteaseɛ no, ɔno a ɔresume no.
examples.note: 'Presumably' kyerɛ sɛ wɔn ani yɛ sɛ ɛyɛ paa, sɛnea 'probablemente' yɛ wɔ Twi.

examples.original: Generally, people prefer to work in the morning.
examples.phonetic: /ˈdʒɛnərəli ˈpiːpəl prɪˈfɜːr tuː wɜːk ɪn ðə ˈmɔːnɪŋ/
examples.translation: Paapaa, mmusua wɔn a wɔde ase bɛka no, wɔpɛ sɛ wɔbɛdi adwuma bere a ɛte morning.
examples.note: 'Generally' kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ trend, nanso ɛnyɛ rule.

levels.label: Modal Verbs for Hedging
levels.translation: Modal verbs a wɔde maa wɔbɛka hedging

examples.original: It might rain later, so take an umbrella.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt maɪt reɪn ˈleɪtər soʊ teɪk ən ʌmˈbrɛlə/
examples.translation: Ebia ɛbɔ bere a ɛbɛba, na sɛ wɔde umbrella ka.
examples.note: 'Might' kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ likely sɛ ɛbɛbɔ sɛ 'may'.

examples.original: Could you help me with this problem?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː hɛlp miː wɪð ðɪs ˈprɒbləm/
examples.translation: Wɔhɔ te sɛ wɔde me kwan ma wɔsolve ɛproblem no?
examples.note: 'Could' maa request no yɛ polite sɛ 'can'.

examples.original: This could be the best option for us.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs kʊd biː ðə bɛst ˈɒpʃən fɔːr ʌs/
examples.translation: ɛyɛ paa sɛ ɛno na ɛyɛ best option ma yɛn.
examples.note: Wɔde 'could' maa wɔbɛsuggest without committing.

levels.label: Impersonal Structures and Tendencies
levels.translation: Impersonal structures na tendencies

examples.original: It seems that the prices have increased significantly.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt siːmz ðæt ðə ˈpraɪsɪz hæv ˈɪnkriːst sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/
examples.translation: Sɛnea yɛte nteaseɛ no, prices no a wɔincrease no paa.
examples.note: Wɔde 'It seems that' + indicative, ɛnni sɛ subjunctive wɔ Twi.

examples.original: I tend to agree with the new policy.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ tɛnd tuː əˈɡriː wɪð ðə njuː ˈpɒləsi/
examples.translation: Mɛtumi aba a mɛkɔ so wɔ new policy no so.
examples.note: 'Tend to' kyerɛ habit anaa tendency, sɛnea 'soler' yɛ wɔ Twi.

examples.original: She appears to be very confident.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː əˈpɪərz tuː biː ˈvɛri ˈkɒnfɪdənt/
examples.translation: Sɛnea ɛte nteaseɛ no, ɔyɛ confident paa.
examples.note: 'Appears to' yɛ ma wɔde maa wɔbɛka asɛm a ɛyɛ sɛnea ɛte nteaseɛ no, sɛnea 'parece' yɛ wɔ Twi.
